newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada details declining borrowing requirements.
newsitem.headline: Canada details declining borrowing requirements.

text.p: The Department of Finance issued a federal debt operations report for 1996 on Friday, detailing the improved fiscal outlook in coming years.

It said the ratio of federal debt to gross domestic product was expected to decline to 74.0 percent in 1997-98 from 75.1 percent in 1996-97, the first meaningful decline in more than two decades, as the result of budget cuts.

"These actions will also reduce the burden of government borrowing in financial markets, lowering financial requirements from C$25.8 billion in 1994-95 to C$6.0 billion in 1997-98," it said in a statement.
Gross federal debt totalled C$623 billion at the end of March. Canada issued C$28.5 billion of new market debt over the 1995-96 fiscal year that ended on March 31.
Market debt accounts for about 75 percent of gross federal debt. The remainder comes from internal sources, principally public service pension plans.
